## 2. Nhật ký tuần

### Tuần 1

**Kế hoạch tuần này là gì?**

Kế hoạch tuần này là gặp anh Tùng vào đầu tuần, dành 2 ngày tham gia đào tạo bán hàng tại trung tâm, sau đó dành thời gian còn lại trong tuần để thực hiện bán hàng.

**Thực tế diễn ra thế nào?**

Mọi thứ gần như diễn ra đúng theo kế hoạch, ngoại trừ việc Khoi bị đuổi khỏi trung tâm vì mặc quần đùi 
Anh Tùng cũng đưa Khỏi đi ăn các món đường phố để tìm hiểu thêm về văn hóa.

**Vì sao khác với kế hoạch?**

Do Khỏi không biết về văn hóa ở đó.

**Tuần sau em làm gì khác?**

Tuần tới, Khỏi sẽ dành nhiều thời gian hơn để tìm hiểu về văn hóa Việt Nam và cố gắng cải thiện vốn từ vựng của mình. Khỏi sẽ đi vắng từ thứ Tư tuần sau

**Tuần này em rút ra quy luật gì?**

Tuần này em rút ra Khỏi cần phải tuân thủ nhất quán các quy định về trang phục FPT và giờ giấc. Ngoài ra, Khoi cũng phải tập thói quen báo cáo không chỉ trên trang web này mà còn với ba Bình và anh Tùng.

**Điều gì khiến em thấy có ý nghĩa?**

Điều mang lại ý nghĩa cho Khoi là việc học hỏi những điều mới mẻ và có những trải nghiệm mới.

## 3. Case 1 – FPT Shop

_Thực tiễn tại nơi thực tập_

### B1 – Hành trình khách hàng

**Tóm tắt tài liệu đọc thêm**

rào cản : customer barrier, worries that cause customers to hesitate when thinking about making a purchase
phá băng: breaking an invisible social barrier between you and the customer to make them feel more comfortable 
điểm chung: finding something you and the customer have in common in order to speak to them as a "friend" when making a sale

For example I was selling to 2 jewish people and know a lot about jewish culture so was able find điểm chung to speak to them about as a "friend" and then was able to sell 1 AirPods and 1 earpod.

**1. [Q] Ba nhóm khách phổ biến nhất ở shop em là ai? Mỗi nhóm đến để giải quyết "việc" gì?**

The first group of customers I would categorize is the ones who only care and want a good price.
I would split this into 2 smaller groups - Foreigners and Vietnamese people.
Foreigners tend to be travelers and tourists, mainly from India, China or European. These customers usually have an idea of the product they need to buy but come in to check the price or if there is any current promotions. This is because Vietnam has one of the cheapest prices for these products compare to that of their home country. For example in Fstudio an iPhone may be up to 200pounds cheaper than in Europe. Hence they come in to buy, with there being additional promotions on certain products. Additionally, we offer roughly- 8% tax refund further lowering the price making buying in Vietnam more appealing. For Vietnamese customers it's a similar situation; they would have done some research on the products but sometimes not much but they also are likely to have done research on prices in comparison to competitors. So they probably have seen that there is a discount on the web and have come into the store looking for the promotions on either the product itself or accessories that come with it to get the best price possible. This helps them feel like they have made a personal victory and created value for themselves by saving money or getting a good deal alongside the strong trust and branding of FPT.


The second group of customers I would categorize is those who go and buy for others - either their family or friends.
The reason they buy for is usually 1 of these 3: children, a friend or gift. The context of the person it is for usually makes the selling part easier. For example, parents who buy for their child; their child is often still studying or now at work. Then depending on what they do we can help offer a solution that matches the specific need and preferences like color which may depend on things like gender or age. Sometimes it is even easier when the person they are buying for already knows what they want or is on the phone directly with the buyer. this makes it easier to ask questions and work together as a team including the customer to find an optimal solution. But overall this group of buyer has a lot of responsibility as they are also trying to create value for someone else so they try to pick the best product with our guide and convincing as sellers so that they can please whoever they be buying for,


The final main group of people I would categorize is Vietnamese people who care mainly about branding and image more than the utility.
I say this is common is Vietnamese people. Although they don't say explicitly out loud, as a seller you can sense that they may not want the product that truly matches their needs the most but rather one that may look good or just the fact that it is an iPhone from apple. Usually as a seller I would actually find the solution that matches their usage and needs the most, but then I get it wrong and they still drift to the best option or a different option. Then the price becomes secondary and the thing like latest model or color matters more to where they are willing to pay a premiem for a specific model or color. Then this gives me the information that they just want the product to solve the problem of things like status, appearance, scarcity. Then I can advise or sell products that match closer to those needs, for example by speaking about the exclusive colors or "trendy", "hot" things that make the customer feel the feeling of scarcity and value externally from the product.

**2. [Q Đ] Hành trình của họ kéo dài bao lâu, qua những điểm chạm nào trước, trong và sau mua? Điểm đau lớn nhất nằm ở đâu?**

The journey can last pretty short from a few minutes to a few hours to even days.

It all depends on what stage of the decision, information and money the customer has. If the customer knows exactly what they want and have the money to purchase it so they it is quick if the seller is able to work efficiently and quick. This could be done is minutes, in and out of the store very fast. However sometimes they can know what they want but don't have the money yet to buy it so they come into the store to experience the product and come back at a later date when they have the money, for example after their salary has been paid.
However some customers may need time to learn more about the product or still have personal worries about whether they really need this product or not or if other places offer better prices. Therefore sometimes the journey can be a few hours, this includes the customer coming in and experiencing the product with the help of the salesperson but ending up leaving. Then potentially after they have made their decision and done their research the customer returns later that day or a few days later to make the purchase.

Common touch points before: 
The customer has an identified problem or need they have to solve eg. a new device for school
Ask family or friends for recommendations 
Compared models, prices, reviews, and promotions online against competitors like DMX
Check what they can afford and whether the product is available maybe through calling FPT 
Done varying amounts of research on product specificaition

Common touchpoints during:
First impressions of store and seller (first 30 seconds)
Greeting and finding out what the customer needs through questions (filter) 
Checking the price, stock, promotions, and payment options. 
Comparing or trying products in person (experience)
Suggesting accessories or asking about warranty and after-sales support eg Zalo Completing payment and receiving the product.

Common touchpoint after:
Setting up or transferring data to the new device 
Learning how to use it or getting help with questions through aftercare like messaging the seller
Returning for service, repairs, warranty support, or accessories if needed

A common pain point is uncertainty: customers may feel overwhelmed by choices or worry they’ll choose the wrong product, pay too much, or payment terms. For customers who already know what they want, the main frustration is often practical—such as the exact model or colour being unavailable, or the purchase taking longer than expected.

**3. [A] Em đã thử thay đổi gì ở một điểm chạm, và kết quả ra sao?**

One point I have tried to change although I have not a lot of experience is the after. 
Once the product has been sold I sometimes see that the customer is not really fully satisfied. This may be either from the price: they don't think it was fully justified or the fact that they are not 100% sure of the products use. This can be seen from the way they react after paying. Therefore I tried to lift the mood by complimenting or telling stories and giving them a picture of what is to come of them using the product. In hopes that they feel more happy and justified about making the purchase instead of regret. The result has been ok nothing major worth noting yet. Maybe need a few more cases to see.

**Tóm tắt tài liệu đọc thêm**

_(chưa trả lời)_

#### 2a. Phễu bán hàng của em

**1. [Q] Phễu bán hàng của em rơi rụng nhiều nhất ở bước nào? Vì sao?**

Most of the time my sales have funneled out for 2 reasons:
Price
The person the buyer is going with doesn't agree with the purchase (often times a family member)

This may be because I have not sold them a good enough reason or benefit to justify the price.
Also because sometimes I targeted the wrong person when trying to make the sale. Sometimes the person is going with matters to the sale more than the actual person buying as they value the opinions of their friends and family highly. While also having to take into account the opinion of the person spending the money.

**2. [Q Đ] So với một nhân viên bán giỏi ở shop, chênh lệch lớn nhất nằm ở bước nào? Họ hỏi khách những câu gì mà em chưa hỏi? Khi tư vấn điện thoại và laptop, loại câu hỏi SPIN nào hiệu quả nhất?**

Compared to a good salesperson at the shop, the biggest difference is their knowledge or product and Vietnamese skills. This helps them be able to tell more stories and sell the experience of the product better than me as they know the product specs better. Combines with superior Vietnamese skills when selling to local customers makes the selling process smoother when talking and convincing. Wheras for me I sometimes really don't know an answer so I have to double check information and with more limited vocabulary makes my sales more choppy and less smooth.

Some questions that they ask guests more often than me is the experience of using the previous or current device that they are using. And from their answer they can read between the lines of what their problems and needs are. I tend to ask more general questions or speak casually with foreign customers

I think Implication questions are most effective. This is because it helps build on emotion and gives more reason and justification to make a purchase. For example when you make in implication you are describing or selling a story and experience that feels more relatable to the customer. Saying things like "this means you can"or asking "does the phone dying mean you're missing calls from customers?" turns the fact of for example a phone having bad battery into an emotional experience. And when you can hit at the customers emotion then it makes it easier to close a deal as their emotions help justify the logic of the purchase (especially women ;).

**3. [Q] Doanh thu mỗi shop tăng có thể đến từ nhiều khách hơn, tỷ lệ chốt cao hơn hoặc đơn lớn hơn. Ở shop em, nguồn nào đóng góp nhiều nhất?**

In Fstudio hai ba trung, according to the manager the high amount of customers is the most important to shop revenue. The combination of good location, big store and solid branding leads many customers especially foreigners to be able to search online and come to the store. And with arithmetics if the store the able to have 20 customers and sell to 10 of them it is still more revenue than a different Fshop that only gets 5 customers.So having higher traffic even returning customers is the most important as it gives the opportunity to good salesmen to close more deals.

#### 2b. Bán hàng cá nhân B2C trong chuỗi bán lẻ

**1. [Q] Khi khách đã tìm hiểu kỹ trên mạng trước khi đến shop, vai trò của người bán tại cửa hàng còn là gì? Em đã tạo thêm giá trị gì mà khách không tự tìm được online?**

When customers have already researched products online before visiting the shop they probably have some good understanding of product. Hence the seller's role is to provide a personal and practical shopping experience. 

To help customers understand the products better, through experience and stories of what value the product can bring instead of just the spec, answer specific questions, and having the skill recommend the most suitable options based on their needs. The value comes from the ability of the seller to give answers to the customer that they cannot find online. Unlike online research, they are allow customers to see, touch, and try the products alongside the sellers guidance in person before making a decision. Its also the trust through face-to-face communication with the seller making customers feel more confident and comfortable with their decisions.

_(chưa trả lời)_

**3. [Đ] Chuỗi chuẩn hóa quy trình bán (kịch bản, chính sách, KPI). Phần nào của việc bán hàng chuẩn hóa được, phần nào phải dựa vào cá nhân người bán? Vì sao một chuỗi cần cả hai?**

Standardization
Every employee should follow a clear structure when serving customers, such as greeting them (Welove), understanding their needs, introducing suitable products, answering questions, and completing the sale. This ensures that every customer receives a professional level of service, regardless of which store they visit. This is done at FPT through the 2 week training at Trung tam dao tao.

Rules in terms of pricing, promotions, discounts, returns, and customer complaints must be consistent across all branches. This prevents confusion, protects the company's reputation, and ensures customers are treated fairly.

Things like store layout and uniforms must also be consistent throughout the branch.
All of this helps maintain a strong brand image and trust for customers which has taken FPT a long time to build.


Individual sellers
Although all employees should follow the same basic sales structure, I believe that each salesperson and customer is different so they should have the flexibility to use their own communication skills, personality which has been gained from the sellers' own life experience when interacting with customers.
This is because there are so many factors such as store location, customer ethnicity, wealth that make each customer different
Different stores in different locations may also have somewhat of their own culture which best suits that geography.
For example, the Fstudio that I work at has many foreign customers.
A good salesperson should be able to recognize these differences and adjust their approach accordingly. It is important for employees to use their own product knowledge and experience to make suitable recommendations depending on each specific situation. This helps create customer loyalty not only to the company  but to the seller themselves.  However, this flexibility must remain within company policies. Employees should never make misleading promises, offer unauthorized discounts, or pressure customers simply to achieve their KPI.

Companies need both because the standardization helps create consistency, efficiency and ensures good consumer experience no matter where they go which helps increase brand image and loyalty. But individual sellers is what makes each store unique and can be the sole reason why customers may choose FPT over competitiors such as DMX although both provide similar products and services at a similar price point.

**4. [Đ P] KPI và thưởng của nhân viên ảnh hưởng thế nào đến cách tư vấn? Có lúc nào KPI kéo người bán đi ngược lợi ích của khách không?**

Kpi and employee rewards affect the method of selling as it acts as an incentive and motivation to reach specific targets. 

KPIs for a store can be reaching a certain amount of revenue or having to sell a certain amount of accessories for example. 

This can affect customers in a negative way sometimes. For example if a store is near their revenue target it may cause employees to try to increase effort to close deals or even upscale customers. If the customers price range is 200$ the salesperson may encourage the customer to buy a 350$ product just to meet to KPI even if the additional costs and features are not necessary. This makes the seller benefit more in comparison to the consumer potentially lowering satisfaction due to the extra spend.
